messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sales discovery - Redwood integration recap

Hi Alex / Sophie,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment. TL;DR: Acme's main goals are (1) improve search relevance & reranking for product docs, (2) reduce latency on chat/assistant experiences to <200ms median, and (3) run a cost-effective POC that proves embeddings + reranking improves conversion for support flows.

Key pain points you called out:
- Current embedding pipeline is slow to refresh (daily) and suffers from inconsistent ranking for multi-paragraph queries.
- Latency spikes on your hosted assistant during peak hours (affects CS response times).
- Fragile SDK hooks in the existing integration (breaking changes with vendor SDKs have caused regressions).

What we covered from Redwood's side (product fit):
- SDKs: lightweight JS/Python clients with a small breaking-change surface; we can pin major versions for the POC. We also offer a server-side Python SDK that supports streaming responses and function-calling payloads.
- Function calling & structured outputs: Redwood supports a function-calling pattern for extracting structured metadata from responses (e.g., intent, entity, doc_id) and returning JSON-friendly outputs for your backend.
- Streaming: low-latency streaming APIs for assistant/chat to hit your <200ms goal under typical load with our recommended batching / cache config.
- Embeddings & reranking: we recommend a hybrid approach — dense embeddings for semantic recall + lightweight heuristic reranker for final sort. We can run an A/B with your top 50k docs.

Action items / next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive / engineering scoping session (30-45m) — propose Wed Oct 27 10am PT. Goal: agree on POC data needs, auth flow, and latency targets.
2) I will share a short integration proposal and data mapping XLS (attached).
3) Redwood engineering (Dev) will produce a preliminary integration checklist and sample function-calling payloads.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, acme-data-mapping-20261020.xlsx

If that all looks right, I'll lock the Wed slot and get a calendar invite out.
\Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

\Marissa — quick engineering note before the deep-dive (copied into invite):
\High-level integration notes / POC plan:
1) Auth & infra
- We support API keys and mTLS for Dedicated/Private customers. For the POC, API keys scoped to a dev env are fine.
\2) SDK/endpoint plan
- JS/Node SDK for the assistant with streaming support (chunked token frames).
- Python server-side SDK for batch embedding generation and reranking helper functions.
- Endpoints:
  - POST /v1/chat/stream (streaming responses, incremental tokens)
  - POST /v1/generate (non-streaming)
  - POST /v1/embeddings (bulk embeddings upsert / query)
  - POST /v1/rerank (optional service to apply learned weights + heuristics)
\3) Function-calling & structured outputs
- We will provide sample schema templates (intent, doc_id, confidence_score, metadata) and a reference payload. Example payload (simplified):
  {"function": "extract_doc_ref", "args": {"query": "..."}}
- Redwood returns a structured JSON block alongside the text stream; our SDK exposes a helper to map that to your backend models.
\4) Embeddings / reranking approach
- Recommend dense embeddings (512d) with an initial index of top 50k docs. Refresh cadence: nightly for initial POC; can move to hourly if you need near-real-time.
- We'll run reranking in two stages: approximate candidate fetch (ANN) + light-weight neural reranker that annotates top 50 candidates. This keeps latency predictable.
\5) POC success metrics
- Rerank lift on CTR / helpfulness >= 8% over baseline on top queries
- p50 assistant latency < 200ms; p95 < 500ms under expected peak QPS (please share numbers)
\I'll bring runnable examples to the deep-dive (simple Node + Python snippets).
\— Dev
